questions.question: Which book is recommended for readers interested in network protocols?
questions.explanation:
The passage explicitly mentions “Computer Networks (Tanenbaum and Wetherall, 2010)” as the suggested book. (Source Page: [27])  

---

questions.question: In the simplified view of the Internet presented, the two kinds of computers are hosts and what?
questions.explanation:
The text states that the Internet consists of “hosts and routers.” (Source Page: [27])  

---

questions.question: According to the passage, most operating systems (e.g., UNIX and Windows) essentially ignore which problem?
questions.explanation:
The passage notes that most OS “basically just ignore the problem” of deadlock/livelock, assuming users prefer occasional livelock over restrictive rules. (Source Page: [29])  

---

questions.question: The passage describes a trade‑off between which two considerations when dealing with deadlock prevention?
questions.explanation:
It explicitly mentions “an unpleasant trade‑off between convenience and correctness.” (Source Page: [29])  

---

questions.question: If a collection of *n* processes each claim 1/*n* of the total resources and then each tries to claim another one, what is the most likely outcome?
questions.explanation:
The text warns that such a scenario could lead to a deadlock, hence it would “not be a good idea.” (Source Page: [29])  

---

questions.question: Why do most operating systems refrain from imposing strict “one process, one open file” restrictions?

options.B: Because the price is high in terms of inconvenient restrictions on processes

questions.explanation:
The passage explains that imposing such restrictions is costly due to the inconvenience they cause. (Source Page: [29])  

---

questions.question: Which of the following statements about deadlocks in communication systems is accurate according to the passage?

options.A: Only communication deadlocks can occur, not resource deadlocks.
options.B: Only resource deadlocks can occur, not communication deadlocks.
options.C: Both communication and resource deadlocks can occur.
options.D: Deadlocks are impossible in modern networks.

questions.explanation:
The text explicitly notes that “not all deadlocks… are communication deadlocks. Resource deadlocks can also occur there.” (Source Page: [27])  

---

questions.question: The “Other Issues” section is identified with which section number?
questions.explanation:
The heading in the passage reads “SEC. 6.7  OTHER ISSUES.” (Source Page: [27])  

---

questions.question: Who are the authors of the referenced “Computer Networks” book?
questions.explanation:
The passage cites the book as authored by “Tanenbaum and Wetherall.” (Source Page: [27])  

---

questions.question: If the problems of deadlock and livelock could be eliminated “for free,” what would likely happen to the discussion surrounding them?

options.A: The discussion would become more intense.

questions.explanation: The passage says that if these problems could be eliminated for free, “there would not be much discussion.” (Source Page: [29])
